query: Are Buried Country and South of the Border both films turned into stage performances?

No, Buried Country and South of the Border are not two separate films that were turned into stage performances. They are two different documentaries created by writer-director Oliver Stone for the 2009 Venice Film Festival.

Buried Country is a highly regarded documentary film about Australian country music in the Aboriginal community, focusing on the genre's most important stars. It was released at the 2009 Venice Film Festival and premiered at the 2009 Venice Film Festival.

South of the Border (1922 film) is a 1922 American silent drama film directed by Paul Powell, which starred Agnes Ayres, Milton Sills, Fred Huntley, Bertram Grassby, Casson Ferguson, Ruby Lafayette, and Sylvia Ashton. It was released at the 2009 Venice Film Festival.

Both films are part of a larger project called "Buried Country: Buried Country is a Highly regarded documentary film", which is a collection of documentaries created by writer-director Oliver Stone for the 2009 Venice Film Festival.

Stone stated that he hopes the film will help people better understand a leader who is wrongly ridiculed "as a strongman, as a buffoon, as a clown."
